rows.synopsis: Ruben moves to a new town, starts at a new school, and discovers something impossible living in his grandfather's bookstore.
rows.situation: Ruben is the new kid again: no skateboarding, no eating in the halls, soup-spilling in front of the most popular kid, and a mom pushing him to make friends while the family grieves near his grandfather's struggling bookstore. Strange writings start appearing with no author, and the kids realize a ghost is communicating only through text.
rows.coping: Curtis's ice pack and a shared Naruto conversation become Ruben's first friendship, and the mystery gives the group a reason to come together. The kids accept that some things cannot be explained yet, name the mystery G.W., and choose to follow the clues instead of walking away.

Then writings appear that nobody wrote, always in words, and the kids work out that a ghost who can only communicate through text is reaching out. The first trail leads them stumbling into a very unexpected tea party.

rows.synopsis: Characters from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland come to life at school, and the kids have to return them to their book while learning why the ghost chose Alice.
rows.situation: The Mad Hatter and the March Hare take over the school, stealing tests and demanding tea, and the kids realize the only way to solve the mystery is to actually read Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. Meanwhile Ruben's grandpa is quietly hurting over the antique cash register his late wife loved, and Chevon starts wondering why the ghost keeps choosing stories about change.
rows.coping: Reading together becomes the tool: understanding the book lets the kids return the characters and see the theme underneath, accepting change. Chevon names what everyone feels, that grieving has more than one way, and the episode lands on the theory that the ghost may be Grandma herself, always with them, before a new message, help me, opens the next mystery.

rows.coping: The kids work the mystery the way Ghostwriter taught them, following clues from termites to ants to the shelter, and Amy and Grandpa find their own compromise about the store. Mowgli's disappearance with the dogs ends the episode on the scariest note yet, Shere Khan may be loose in the city, and the team chooses to keep going.

Avery Boyd's game is beaten, Layla Barnes is restored, and Oliver is released to peace by the friends he made on purpose. The last scenes trade case for community, a thank-you, a tear, a third controller, and the show's real answer to who have we been talking to: someone who wanted us to find each other.
